# YM14: 武陵春色 Wuling Chunse, "Spring Colors at Wu Ling"

Malone calls it Peach Blossom Cave.

Wave 1 · Yuanming Yuan · 3D: `/reconstruction/3d.html?b=YM14` · Page: `/scenes/#YM14` · Row: `research/buildings/YM14-wuling-chunse/`

## What it was

武陵春色 Wuling Chunse, "Spring Colours of Wuling", the peach-blossom valley reached over a bridge behind 万方安和, east and a little north, south of a rock tunnel (S05 j81:12b; E1492). Finished 1726 after Tao Yuanming's Peach Blossom Spring; first named 桃花坞 as a whole; Qianlong lived and read here as a prince from 1726 and called his study 乐善堂 before moving to 长春仙馆 (S05 j81:13a; E1492; S361 v2 p.132; E1500). The visitor came by boat up the stream through the cave 壶中天 to a pool with its halls (E1500; S02 p.81; E1499). Under Jiaqing 恒春堂 was added for theatre, with the two-storey stage 壶中仙籁 (S43 1.8; E1501; E1513, E1514). Burned in October 1860.

From the inventory row: **built** 建于1720年前, 初名桃花坞 (S42); by 1722: 桃花塢 and 壺中天 named in a prince's poems (雍邸集); before 1720, as 桃花坞; 1726; **changed** 桃花坞 theatre added 1811 (S43); differs on later plans (S41); 1726 (雍正四年): Qianlong studies here and names it 樂善堂; earlier the whole was 桃花塢; **destroyed** 1860 (S05, S02, S08, S41, S42, S43, S01, S200, S340, S361).

## The scene itself

### The leaf of 1744, its poem and preface

Leaf 14 of the 1744 album. Qianlong's preface: "循溪流而北複谷環抱山桃萬株" (following the stream north, valleys fold round, with ten thousand mountain peach trees). Petals fall and float on the water; at dawn and dusk the trees blaze like snow and flushed cloud. The quatrain: "複岫迴環一水通", ring upon ring of hills with one stream through them (S40, printed in S05 j81:14b-15a; E1472).

### How later sources differ

日下旧闻考 lists, from the cave: 武陵春色 with 壶中日月长 north of the pool, 天然佳妙 to the east and 洞天日月多佳景 on the south porch; 全璧堂 to the west with the pavilion 小隐栖迟 south-east; behind, through a gap in the hills, 清秀亭 east and 清会亭 west; 桃花坞 north, 清水濯缨 its west room, 桃源深处 further west; 绾春轩 east of the 坞 and 品诗堂 north-east of the 轩 (S05 j81:12b-13a; E1492). The editors add the five-bay 天君泰然 and, under Jiaqing, 恒春堂 (S361; E1500). Jiaqing wrote on 恒春堂 in 1812 and 1813 (E1513, E1514); plays are on record at its stage in 1819 and 1839 (S43; E1501).

Only a short record without catalogue data (S310 rec. 2812; E1504): built before 1720 as 桃花坞, a rock tunnel in the south-east entered by boat, halls 壶中日月长 (five-bay open hall north of the pool), 天然佳妙, 洞天日月多佳景, 桃源深处, 绾春轩, 品诗堂. No drawing number seen; the 初编 has pp.267-286 on it (E1503).

## Interior and setting

### Interior

Plaques: inside the cave 壶中天; 壶中日月长, 天然佳妙, 洞天日月多佳景, 小隐栖迟, 清秀, 清会亭, 桃花坞, 清水濯缨, 桃源深处 in Yongzheng's hand; 全璧堂, 绾春轩, 品诗堂 in Qianlong's (S05 j81:13a-13b; E1492). The stage carried 天上云璈 and 壶中仙籁 (S43; E1501). 品诗堂 is where Qianlong had studied and written as a young man (E1511, E1512).

| Row | Kind | What | Source | Quote or basis | Grade | Seen |

| YM14-15 | plaque | 天上云璈 and 壶中仙籁 on the stage | S43 section 1.8 | E1501 | B | snippet |

### The garden around it

A closed valley of hills round a stream, ten thousand peach trees on the slopes (E1472). A canal passes through a cave under the hill on the east side and out on the other (S02 p.81; E1499). Willows at 绾春轩 ("百尺垂丝绿影铺", E1509; "柳色微黄", E1510). Birdsong and dogs barking beyond the stream in the poem on 桃源深处 (E1508).
